lessons.title: Why Controlling Others Exhausts You
lessons.key_idea: Most of our frustration comes from trying to control people, and simply saying let them frees up the energy we waste on what we cannot change.
issues: scene 1: A lone indigo dot floats between Mel's head and the PHOTOS card. It reads as a stray artifact rather than a thought bubble. (fix: Either remove the dot or complete it as a thought-bubble trail (2-3 dots of increasing size) leading from Mel's head to the photo and dinner cards.)

scene 8: The closing scene is almost entirely text. The only visual is a small '?' badge in the top right, leaving the right half of the stage largely empty. (fix: Add a simple illustration on the right, such as the 'you' figure with lines to several indigo figures, where the lines fade or detach to show letting go. Keep the question text on the left.)

lessons.title: Let Them, Then Let Me
lessons.key_idea: Letting others act is only half the method, because your real power lies in deciding how you will respond.

lessons.title: Let Them Think What They Think
lessons.key_idea: Other people's opinions of you are outside your control, and you do not need their approval to live your life.

lessons.title: Their Feelings Are Theirs, Yours Are Yours
lessons.key_idea: You cannot control how others feel or react, but you can manage your own emotions and choose a calm, deliberate response.

lessons.title: Invest in People Who Show Up
lessons.key_idea: How people behave tells you who they are, so instead of chasing or begging you can let some drift and give your energy to those who make an effort.

lessons.title: Turn Comparison Into Direction
lessons.key_idea: When others succeed or move faster, let them, and use that feeling as a signal to focus on your own goals.
issues: scene 2: The 'THEM' and 'YOU' race-lane labels are tiny monospace text, about 16px at 1600 width. They are below the 18px minimum and hard to read. (fix: Increase the lane labels to at least 20px and place them clearly beside or above each dot.)

scene 7: The 'LUCK', 'STARTING POINT' and 'PAST' labels inside the dashed circle are very small, low-contrast grey text, roughly 18px or less. They are barely legible. (fix: Raise these labels to 20-22px and use the darker muted grey-blue or ink navy for better contrast.)

lessons.title: Pause, Let Them, Let Me
lessons.key_idea: A simple routine ties it all together: pause, say let them, name what is in your control, and then choose your next move.

plan.title: The Let Them Theory
plan.author: Mel Robbins
plan.confidence_note: I know the book's central Let Them and Let Me idea and its general themes, but not its chapter-by-chapter content, so this plan relies mainly on the source notes provided.
plan.one_liner: Stop wasting energy controlling other people, and put it into the one response you control.
plan.summary: Mel Robbins argues that much of our stress comes from trying to control things we never could, like other people's choices, moods, opinions and timelines. When someone leaves us out, runs late, criticises us or simply doesn't make an effort, our instinct is to fix, chase or convince them. Her answer is two simple phrases. First, let them: accept that people are free to act as they choose. Second, let me: decide what you will do in response. This shift hands your time, energy and peace back to you. Robbins applies it to friendships, relationships, other people's opinions, comparison and emotions. People's behaviour becomes useful information about where to invest yourself, and you can turn someone else's success into a cue to work on your own goals. The result is a calmer, more deliberate way to live.
